title: A typed title passes and an untyped one is refused with its reason, by --title, a message file and the commit-msg hook on main, while a branch's commits stay free-form
when: Checks typed, untyped and wrongly typed titles, by --title and a message file, then in a temporary git repo with the hook enabled commits on main, on a branch, and a squash merge of the branch into main.
then: Expects typed titles to pass and every other title refused with its reason; on main the hook refuses an untyped commit and the untyped squash and takes the typed squash, and on the branch it takes a free-form commit.

title: The migrations are numbered in order and recorded as applied
when: Applies the migrations to a fresh database.
then: Expects them numbered 1, 2, 3 and so on, each recorded with its name.

title: The schema read back loads each stored table after the tables it points at
when: Reads the schema's load order and foreign keys.
then: Expects every stored table a foreign key points at to come before it.

title: Removing a product kind while a record of it is left is refused
when: Opens a store whose product declares the kind `memo` under a domain and holds the record EX-LEND-M01 of it, then removes the `memo` product kind.
then: Expects the removal refused, naming `memo`.

title: The server has no way to change the meta-model
when: Sends POST and PUT requests to the meta model's read, `/api/meta-model/get-meta-model`, and to schema-like paths, and a write to a meta table, on the running server.
then: Expects them refused, and the migrations unchanged.

title: A schema change written as the next numbered migration is applied on the next load, and the data is checked against it
when: Writes a migration that adds a column on a copy of the package, regenerates the row types and the reference, and loads data that uses it.
then: Expects the data refused before the migration, accepted after it, and the same data refused by the unchanged package.

title: The row types in src/store/tables.ts match the schema
when: Renders the row types from the schema description.
then: Expects them to equal the committed `lathe/src/platform/data/tables.ts`.

title: Every kind has an ID in the registry, a title and its parent columns
when: Reads every kind's table and parents from the schema description.
then: Expects each kind's table keyed by `id`, with a foreign key from `id` into `record_id`, a required title and a foreign key for each parent column; a lone parent column required, and two or three parent columns all optional with a CHECK that exactly one is given.

title: Each relation's pairs fit its link table's ends
when: Reads every relation's pairs and every supertype's members from the schema description.
then: Expects every relation to have pairs, each pair's kinds accepted by the link table's ends or their supertypes, and every supertype member a kind.

title: Which kinds are obligations, and which links design or prove a product's own obligation, come from the schema
when: Loads a product with its own obligation kind, with a design relation, a proof relation and one with no role.
then: Coverage lists exactly the kinds flagged as obligations; a record reached by the design and proof relations is designed and proved, one reached only by the relation with no role is neither.

title: Each kind the schema flags as an obligation is a member of the obligation supertype, and only those
when: Reads the schema's kinds and supertypes.
then: Expects the obligation supertype to be exactly Lathe's ten obligation kinds.

title: The schema describes every table and every column of a stored table
when: Reads every table and column in the schema description.
then: Expects a description on every table, and on every column of a stored table that is not a link table.

title: The schema version is one whole number in schema/version.json, and each converter moves the data forward one version
when: Reads schema/version.json and Lathe's own converters, then a folder of converters with one that skips a version.
then: Expects SCHEMA_VERSION to be the file's number, Lathe's converters to chain from 1 to it one version each, and a converter that skips a version refused.

title: 1-to-2 puts every flow through its product's one new interface, renaming its flows, steps and tests wherever they are named
when: Runs every converter from 1 on a committed product at schema 1 with a flow, its step and test, a fulfills link and a requirement whose text names the step.
then: Every ID and mention ends in FL01 after 1-to-2, the flow going through the new TL-IF01, internal; 3-to-4 then merges it back into the use case's one flow, offered through TL-IF01; the data is at this Lathe's schema, and the to-dos say what is left.

title: 1-to-2 gives every test one of the five levels, and a manual test the level that fits its kind
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of each test kind at the seven old levels, manual among them.
then: database becomes integration, api and contract service, e2e-api system, e2e-ui browser; a manual flow, view, use case or policy test browser, any other the lowest level its kind allows, with a to-do to check it.

title: 1-to-2 puts every repository under its aggregate's domain, persisting that aggregate, renamed wherever it is named
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of repositories under their aggregates, in two domains, one named by a link, a part and a text.
then: Each repository sits under its aggregate's domain as <domain>-REPO<nn>, numbered in its aggregates' order, with a persists link to its one aggregate; the link, the part and the text name the new ID, and the to-dos say to split a class that persists several aggregates into one repository each, and to rename the IDs in code.

title: 1-to-2 drops the descriptions that are gone, opens each When with its Given, and stands in for each required text a record lacks
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of two commands (one without a description), a data model with a description, a flow step, and two invariant tests with a Given, one without a When.
then: Expects the data model's description gone and the step with none, each Given opening its test's When (or becoming it), the command without a description given "To write: what it changes and when it is refused.", the three changes counted, and one to-do naming TL-LEND-CMD02's description.

title: 1-to-2 puts each command under its aggregate's root entity, and leaves a to-do for an aggregate with none
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on a command of an aggregate with a root entity and one of an aggregate with none.
then: Expects the first under the root entity (entity_id in place of aggregate_id), the second left as it was with a to-do naming it, and the to-do to move commands that change a child entity.

title: 1-to-2 drops every recorded exception and waiver, and leaves a to-do to change the model
when: Runs the 1-to-2 converter's files phase on raw rows of a command change, a repository share, a pattern rule with its setting and applies-when condition, and a setting value with a not-applicable reason.
then: The command change and the repository share are gone, the rule keeps only its own columns, the reason is the setting's value, and the to-dos name each one to change in the model.

title: 2-to-3 gives each check the domain of its check_row record, removes the check_row records and kind, and leaves a to-do for a check no record names
when: Runs the 2-to-3 converter's files phase on raw rows of two checks, one check_row record naming the first, and the check_row kind with its fields.
then: The first check has its domain_id, the check_row records, kind and fields are gone, and the to-do names the second check and the fix.

title: 2-to-3 leaves a to-do for every check of a product with no check_row records
when: Runs the 2-to-3 converter's files phase on raw rows of one check and no check_row records.
then: The check is unchanged, nothing is reported as changed, and the to-do names the check.

title: 2-to-3 does nothing to data that is already upgraded
when: Runs the 2-to-3 converter's files phase on a check that has its domain_id.
then: No table changes and there are no changes or to-dos.

title: 3-to-4 gives each product kind its complexity from its stage, makes each standard engineering with a to-do to review it, gives each product setting no technology words, and makes each interface internal with a to-do to mark the public ones
when: Runs the 3-to-4 converter's files phase on product kinds of the technical specification, the test plan, interface design and no stage, a standard with no type, a product setting with no technology words and an interface that says nothing of being public.
then: Each product kind is accidental, as-parent, essential and essential; the standard is engineering with a to-do naming it to review as a quality; the setting lists no words; the interface is internal with a to-do naming it to mark public where it is; four changes are reported.

title: 3-to-4 does nothing to data that is already upgraded
when: Runs the 3-to-4 converter's files phase on a product kind with its complexity, a standard with its type, a setting with its technology words and a public interface.
then: No table changes and there are no changes or to-dos.

title: 3-to-4 drops a product's declaration of a provided_by, fills or generates pair its own kind now has, as Lathe's kinds have them, and keeps every other
when: Runs the 3-to-4 converter's files phase on an accidental kind and an obligation kind whose product declares their fills, generates and provided_by pairs, beside a provided_by pair with the product's kind as provider and another relation.
then: Only the declarations of the pairs the kinds now have are dropped, with one change naming each.

title: 3-to-4 merges a use case's flows into one, keeping the union of their steps, marking variants, and reports what it cannot merge
when: Runs 3-to-4 on a use case with a web app flow and a CLI flow, each with a step invoking the same command, one step of its own each, a view the web steps happen in, and a test each.
then: Expects one flow titled as the use case; the shared step once with both requirements; each flow's own step a variant of its interface; the view presenting the command; both interfaces offering the use case; the automated system test kept as the flow's, the other gone and what named it renamed; and to-dos for the gone test, the variants, the step whose view is lost and the interfaces' roles.

title: 4-to-5 changes no row, asks to rename a product's own kind or relation that clashes with a new table, and to write the journey each duration outcome times
when: Runs the 4-to-5 converter's files phase on a product kind named journey, two pairs of a product relation named carries_out beside another relation, and three outcomes whose measures are a share, a median of days from one moment to another, and how long something takes.
then: No table changes and no changes are reported; one to-do names the kind and the relation once to rename, and one names the two duration outcomes to write journeys for.

title: 4-to-5 tells a product with no journeys where they go, and says nothing to one that has them
when: Runs the 4-to-5 converter's files phase on a product with one outcome and no journeys, then on the same product with a journey.
then: The first gets one to-do saying journeys arrive in Discovery; the second no table changes, no changes and no to-dos.

title: 5-to-6 numbers each product's domains from 1 in ID order, the numbers inside IDs compared by value, and changes nothing else
when: Runs the 5-to-6 converter's files phase on domains of two products, one with IDs XX-D2 and XX-D10, then on data with no domains.
then: Each domain gains position after product_id, numbered from 1 within its product (D2 before D10); other tables are unchanged; the first run reports one change, the second none.

title: 6-to-7 moves each product kind in interaction-design to interface-design, keeps its other fields and every other kind, and does nothing to data already upgraded
when: Runs the 6-to-7 converter's files phase on a product kind in interaction-design and one in technical-specification, then again on the converted data.
then: The first kind is in interface-design with its other fields as they were, the second unchanged, one change reported naming the kind and no to-dos; the second run changes nothing and reports nothing.

title: 7-to-8 gives each use case the result its flow's main path invokes, lists a split for several commands, a merge for a shared first actor and result, and a use case that invokes nothing, and does nothing to data already upgraded
when: Runs the 7-to-8 converter's files phase on use cases whose main paths invoke one command after a query, two queries the last a variant, two commands then a query, nothing (with a command on another path), and a command another use case of the product's same first actor takes, and one in another product; then again once each has a result.
then: The first takes its command, the second the last query, the third the later command with a split to-do, the fourth none with a to-do, the fifth its command with a merge to-do naming the earlier, the other product's none; the column sits after goal, the changes count each rule, and the second run changes nothing.

title: 8-to-9 puts each use case in its capability's domain, gives each capability's outcomes to its use cases' aggregates and read models, removes the capabilities, lists what only a person can settle, stops at a kind built on capabilities, and does nothing to data already upgraded
when: Runs the 8-to-9 converter's files phase on use cases in capabilities that serve outcomes, one capability with no use case, one use case whose result is another domain's, an about link to a capability, a check that reads the capability table and a text naming a capability; on a product kind and a relation built on capabilities; then again on the converted data.
then: Each use case takes its capability's domain in the column's place, each aggregate and read model serves the outcomes of its use cases' capabilities once, journeys' rows stay, the capability table is empty, and the to-dos name each thing a person settles; the kind built on capabilities stops the upgrade with nothing changed; the second run changes nothing.

title: A record is one row of its kind's table, with typed columns, and its links are rows of their relations' tables
when: Loads a clean product's data.
then: Expects a use case with its typed columns, its parent, product and domain, and its actor as a part row, a domain rule's statement, an applies link as a row, and no problems.

title: Data files hold one JSON object per line, sorted by key, columns in table order
when: Writes the fixture's rows into an empty data folder through the store's add and link commands.
then: Expects one object per line, rows sorted by key with numbers as numbers, columns in the table's order, empty columns left out, and a trailing newline.

title: Data files keep text as UTF-8, and a table file goes when its last row goes
when: Sets the product's icon and description to text with an emoji, accents and curly quotes, then removes the last link of a table.
then: Expects text kept as UTF-8, and no file for a table whose last row is removed.

title: A line that is not JSON, a column the table lacks and a file for no table are named by file and line
when: Loads data with a line that is not JSON, a row with a column its table lacks, and a file named for no table.
then: Expects each refused, naming its file and line.

title: A product with a record of every kind loads each record as one row of its table
when: Loads the fixture with a record of every kind and a row of every stored table.
then: Expects every row in its table.

title: A data file's line order and each line's column order do not change what it means, and a file that is not <table>.jsonl is ignored
when: Copies the complete example library's data with each file's lines reversed and each line's fields reversed, next to a README.md, and loads the copy.
then: Expects the same records, links and coverage, and no problems.

title: Data files are the same bytes whatever order the rows were written in
when: Writes the same rows in two orders, then reloads and rewrites them.
then: Expects the same bytes each time.

title: Each test is of the test kind named after what it tests, and sits under that one record, which it proves
when: A use case test is removed, or written under another requirement.
then: Each test kind has one required parent named by its kind; only that requirement goes unproved.

title: Nothing the Reader is looking at jumps
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: Open a page; move between records by the nav, a link, the graph, Back and quick find; collapse and resize the wiki card and the panels, fold rows, move around the graph and the ERD; reload while scrolled; open a tooltip and the overlays; switch the theme; and on a phone open and close the sheets.
then: Nothing on screen moves unless the Reader moved it: the nav, the page bar and the header strip stay put, the reload comes back at the same scroll, and the tooltip, overlays and sheets open where they show without pushing the page.

title: Move around a record with nothing jumping
when: Follows a link and goes Back. Opens the Graph pane and uses Expand all. Zooms the graph, and resizes the panes by dragging. Changes the record through the CLI while the page is open. Opens and closes quick find, and switches the theme.
then: Expects each move to stay within the layout-shift budget with its frame holding still. The performance budgets are judged by the performance suites.

title: Performance: big maps pan and zoom at 60 Hz, frame a walked focus within 200 ms, and lay out off the main thread, through a reload
when: On the production build over the large product, pans and zooms the Graph, the ERD and the Trace, walks the Graph's focus with the arrow keys, and pans the Graph while a CLI write changes a use case's title.
then: Expects no frame over 20 ms while panning and zooming each stage and through the reload, each walked focus framed within 200 ms, and the Graph's map laid out in the layout's worker within 4 s.

title: The Reader reads and moves around Lathe on a phone
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: On a phone, open Lathe, search for a use case by its ID, switch to the Graph, pinch and open a node, use the wiki card sheet, the nav sheet and the Open pages sheet; then use a tablet in landscape.
then: Text is readable without zooming, every target is large enough for a finger, no page scrolls sideways, the search opens the use case, the graph pans and pinches and opens the node, and each sheet opens and closes; on the tablet the panels show side by side.

title: Read the spec on a phone
when: At 375 by 812 with touch, opens quick find from the top bar and taps a use case. Taps Graph in the page bar and pinches out: the camera zooms in. Taps a node, which opens it. Swipes the wiki card sheet to full height, then away. Opens the nav sheet and chooses the domain; Back, twice, takes them back to the use case. At tablet landscape size: the workbench, with targets at least 40 px tall.
then: Expects each touch to do what it does on a phone, and the workbench on a tablet.

title: The Reader uses Lathe by keyboard and screen reader
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: With a screen reader on and only the keyboard, tab round the nav, the tab panel, the wiki card and the stage, open records, switch stages and collapse the wiki card, pick High contrast in light and dark, and open a dialog and a phone sheet.
then: Every control is reached by Tab in order with a visible focus ring and announced by its name and state, records open and stages switch from the keyboard, High contrast passes in light and dark, and focus moves into the dialog and the sheet and returns when they close.

title: Use Lathe with a keyboard and a screen reader
when: Tabs round: the nav, the page bar, the stage and the wiki card are reached. Opens a record by quick find: focus is not dropped. Opens Graph and collapses the wiki card: the announcer names each change. Picks High contrast by keyboard. Opens the palette: Tab stays inside; Escape gives focus back to its opener.
then: Expects every region reached, each change announced and focus held and returned.

title: The Reader works the whole app from the keyboard
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: In the app, with a screen reader on, press Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P and run commands from the palette and by their VS Code keys, Cmd/Ctrl+B among them; type in a search box; press ? and change a shortcut's key in the sheet.
then: Every command runs from its key and from the palette, the screen reader announces what changed, typing in a search box never fires a single-key shortcut, and the new key runs its command at once and after a reload, and shows in the shortcuts sheet.

title: Work the app from the keyboard
when: Opens the palette with Ctrl+Shift+P and finds a command with its keys. Hides and shows the navigation with Ctrl+B; the announcer speaks. Types g, t and ? in a filter box: they type and open nothing. Presses ?: the shortcuts sheet by group, with its search and a key to add to each shortcut.
then: Expects each command run by its keys and no shortcut firing while typing.

title: The Reader learns a shortcut where it is used
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: Rest on a control that has a shortcut, open the palette and the shortcuts sheet, and reach the control with a screen reader; then change its key in the sheet and look again.
then: The tooltip, the palette, the shortcuts sheet and the screen reader (`aria-keyshortcuts`) each give the same keys, and after the change each gives the new keys.

title: See each command's shortcut where it is used
when: Rests on the Graph button: its tooltip names its keys, which aria-keyshortcuts also carries. Reads a command's keys in the palette. Changes the navigation's Ctrl+B to Ctrl+J in the shortcuts sheet. Reads Ctrl+J in the tooltip and aria-keyshortcuts at once and after a reload, then in the palette, and runs it.
then: Expects every hint to follow the rebinding, and the new key to run the command.

title: The Reader works under Lathe's own title bar
manual_reason: Only the app shows it: a person uses the app as the Reader does.
when: In the desktop app, go back and forward from the title bar, click the command center, show and hide the navigation, drag the bar and double-click it, then change the theme.
then: Back and forward move through the history, the command center opens quick find, the navigation hides and shows, dragging the bar moves the window and a double-click zooms it, and the bar follows the new theme with no flash.

title: The title bar in a real window
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the window's own controls and the system's gestures, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/chrome.ts` or `app/src/shell/DesktopTitleBar.tsx`.
when: Run `npm --prefix desktop start`. The window has no system title bar; the traffic lights sit centered in Lathe's bar, clear of the back button. Drag the bar between its controls: the window moves. Double-click it there: the window zooms (or minimizes, if the system's setting says so). Click each control: it acts and the window does not move. Narrow the window: the command center shortens with an ellipsis and stays centered on the window. Choose another theme and switch between light and dark: the bar and the window's background follow, with no flash.
then: It passes when every step behaves as written.

title: The menus run the page's commands
manual_reason: Only macOS shows the native menu bar: a person checks it in the built app.
when: Open the menu bar in the desktop app and choose View items that stand for the app's commands.
then: The menus are File, Edit, View, Window and Help, and each View item does what its key does in the page.

title: The page in the desktop app finds window.latheDesktop, so it knows it runs there
when: Runs the real shell, hidden, on a small product folder and reads `window.latheDesktop.isDesktop` in the page.
then: Expects `window.latheDesktop.isDesktop` to be true.

title: The native menus, and a View item run by its command ID
when: Runs the real desktop shell, hidden, on a small product. Reads the application menu's top-level labels and the View menu's items. Sends View, Show or Hide Navigation by its command ID. Reads window.latheDesktop.isDesktop.
then: Expects File, Edit, View, Window and Help after the app menu, the View items, the navigation folded and the page knowing it runs in the desktop app. macOS only, as the whole smoke run.

title: A second launch or a folder opened from Finder goes to the running app
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: With the packed app running, runs `open -a Lathe ~/some/product` or drags a product folder onto the Dock icon, then does it again.
then: The running app opens the folder in a window, and the second time brings that window forward; no second app starts.
notes: T124 routes a second launch at unit level.

title: The window has no spell check, overlay scroll bars and native context menus, and reopens in full screen
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: In the desktop app, scrolls a long page, right-clicks in quick find, then enters full screen, quits and reopens.
then: The scroll bars float over the page, the right-click offers Cut, Copy and Paste, and the window comes back in full screen with the title bar's back button at the left edge.

title: A killed run leaves macOS no window state to offer to reopen
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: Force quits Lathe while it opens its window, then opens it again.
then: macOS does not offer to reopen windows; Lathe opens its own last folder.
notes: T127 (`desktop/test/persistence.test.ts`) checks the defaults at unit level.

title: The shell opts out of macOS window restoration, on a Mac and for a test harness's Electron
when: Starts the shell on macOS, elsewhere, and as a test harness runs the unpacked Electron.
then: Expects ApplePersistenceIgnoreState and NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows set on macOS and for the harness, and nothing elsewhere.

title: The Dock, the app menu and the error page behave as a Mac app's
manual_reason: Only macOS shows the Dock and the app menu: a person checks them in the built app.
when: Keep Lathe in the Dock with a folder that has check errors and one the engine cannot load; open the Dock menu, About Lathe and Settings…
then: The icon reads at every size, the badge counts the front window's errors, the Dock menu opens a folder and lists the recent ones, About shows the versions, Settings… opens Appearance, and the folder that cannot load opens the error page saying why.

title: A native Mac app at the screen
manual_reason: Manual because it watches the Dock, Finder, the system's menus and the look of the icon, which only a person at the screen sees. Run it after changing `desktop/src/main.ts`, `desktop/build/icon.svg` or `app/src/shell/desktopRecord.tsx`.
when: Run `npm --prefix desktop run dev`: the Dock shows the icon with a DEV band. Run `npm --prefix desktop run pack` and open the app from `desktop/release/`: the icon is crisp in the Dock, in Finder's list view (16 px) and in Cmd+Tab, in light and in dark appearance. Open a folder whose checks report errors: the Dock badge shows their number. Fix one: the badge follows. Bring a window with no errors forward: the badge clears. Right-click the Dock icon: New Window opens the folder picker, and the recent folders are listed (packed app). Choose Lathe › About Lathe: a small window shows the versions; Source Code and Reference open in the browser. Press Cmd+,: the focused window shows Settings. On a record, click Reveal in Finder, Open in editor and Copy ID in its facts, and right-click a record row, a graph node and the page title: the native menu offers the same three and each works. With the app running, run `open -a Lathe ~/some/product` (packed app) or drag a product folder onto the Dock icon: the running app opens it, and a second time brings its window forward. Open a new folder: the window shows the shell color and "Opening <product>…" at once, never white. Break a row of one of its data files and reopen the folder: the error page shows the message; fix it and click Retry. Scroll a long page: the scroll bars float over it. Right-click in quick find: Cut, Copy and Paste. Enter full screen, quit and reopen: the window comes back in full screen, and the title bar's back button sits at the left edge. Force quit Lathe while it opens its window, then open it again: macOS does not ask to reopen windows.
then: It passes when every step behaves as written.
notes: The nav keeps the theme's own color: the system's sidebar material was left out, since it needs a transparent window and nav, which would replace every theme's nav color with the system's gray and give up the shell color that keeps a new window from flashing.

title: Every stage, view and kind of record page measures clean on four phones
when: Opens every stage, every view over the stage and one record of each kind, its page in the wiki card's sheet, at 375 × 812, 390 × 844, 430 × 932 and 812 × 375 with touch, waits for each page's own signals that it is ready (fonts loaded, nothing busy, animations finished, every box still over three looks), and measures it with the five phone checks.
then: Expects no page wider than the screen, no text cut off without an ellipsis and its whole text as a name, no target under 44 × 44 px outside a sentence, no two targets over each other or one under a fixed bar, and no target scrolling cannot reach.
notes: Run with npm --prefix app run test:mobile, and in the browser batch (scripts/ci.sh --browser); each finding names its element, its phone and a cropped screenshot, gathered in app/mobile/results/.

title: Each phone check finds the broken element on a fixture page and passes the sound one
when: On fixture pages at 375 × 812 with touch, measures a page with content past the screen's edge, cut-off text, small targets, small targets with a hit box stretched past them (wide enough, too short, and one a neighbor covers), overlapping targets and a fixed bar, and targets clipped away, beside sound ones of each.
then: Expects each check to report exactly the broken elements, and none inside a pannable map.
notes: Run with npm --prefix app run test:mobile-measure: fixture pages only, no server.

title: An aggregate with more entities than the limit is a warning naming it, the count and the limit
when: An aggregate has more entities than max_entities_per_aggregate.
then: aggregate-too-large names it, its count and the limit.

title: No query handler or projection imports a repository or an aggregate's model, and a handler reads only through its reader
when: Reads the imports and code of each converted slice's queries.ts, read-model.ts and reader.ts, every file that imports a reader, and the reader records.
then: Expects none of them to import a repository.ts or the aggregate's model type or row builder from its model.ts; each query handler to be given its reader by the runner and to take only types from its read model; the reader not to read source rows; a reader imported only by its own slice's queries.ts; and each read model to have one reader record naming that reader.ts.

title: A meaning that uses another term's title without a builds_on link is a warning
when: Terms use other terms' titles in their meanings: whole and plural, inside a longer term's title, inside another word, in backticks, and one already linked with builds_on.
then: term-used-unlinked warns only of the whole and plural uses with no link, naming the term used.

title: A domain's glossary lists each term after every term it builds on, otherwise by title
when: Terms are added with builds_on links, one through a term of another domain, and the domain is read with get-domain.
then: Its terms come bottom-up, ties by title, each with the terms it builds on.

title: The wiki and the nav list a domain's terms after the terms they build on, otherwise by title
when: Terms are added to a domain, one building on another listed after it by title, and the domain's folders are read.
then: The term folder lists them bottom-up: Basket, Mango, Zebra, then Apple, which builds on Zebra.

title: An aggregate, read model or obligation no outcome reaches is a serves-no-outcome warning
when: Loads the complete product, then the same with no aggregate or read model serving an outcome.
then: Expects no warning, then a serves-no-outcome warning for each aggregate, read model and obligation, saying to write the use case that needs it or remove it.

title: A business outcome whose target says no date is an outcome-target-undated warning
when: Loads the complete product with its outcome's target given with no date, then with a year and with a span from an event.
then: Expects one outcome-target-undated warning naming the outcome, then none.

title: Only a composition nests; every other parent is a link
when: Asks the composition rule about each composed pair and a set of parent pairs that are links.
then: Expects each composed pair, tests included, to nest, and none of the others.

title: In the Map every record sits in an area or inside the record it is part of, once
when: Lays out the test product's Map and the grouped workspace's.
then: Expects every record once, every record inside a record to be its parent's composition, and every composed child inside its parent.

title: A step that invokes a command other than its use case's result is an error on any path, whoever its subject is, and a write that adds one is refused
when: A use case whose result is Borrow a tool has steps in which the librarian adds a tool, the member borrows it, the member sees the free tools, and, on a refused path, the member adds a tool; a query use case has a step that borrows a tool; then a step of the complete product is linked to a second command, and a use case's result is changed to a query while its step borrows a tool.
then: use-case-invokes-another-command reports the two Add a tool steps, naming the command and the result, and not the query; it reports the query use case's command step; and both writes are refused with it.

title: A use case whose main path never invokes its result, through an interface that offers it, is an error
when: A use case whose result is Borrow a tool has a main path that only sees the free tools, the borrow on another path; another invokes its result only in the web app's variant and is offered by a kiosk too; a third has no flow.
then: use-case-result-not-invoked reports the first through the web app and the second through the kiosk, and not the third, which is left to its gap.

title: A query use case whose main path's last invoking step asks something other than its result is an error; a command use case may ask after its result
when: A query use case asks its result, then a second query; the same steps with the second query as the result; and with the result never asked. The complete product's command use case asks a query after its command.
then: use-case-not-done reports the first, naming the last step and what it invokes, and none of the others.

title: Two use cases of a product with the same first actor and result are an error, and a write that makes them so is refused
when: A member's use case with the same result as Borrow a tool is added, and a librarian's with the member second; then the store is asked to add the member's, and to make the member first in the librarian's.
then: use-case-identity-taken reports the member's on load, naming the earlier use case, and not the librarian's; both writes are refused with it.

title: A command use case whose title does not start with its command's verb is a warning; a query use case is not read
when: Borrow a tool is retitled borrow A tool with spaces around, then Lend a tool, then See the free tools with a query as its result.
then: use-case-title-off-result warns only of Lend a tool, naming the command's title and verb.

title: Each record's product and domain come from its parents, and refused data is a data-refused error
when: Loads the good fixture and reads the product, domain, aggregate and parent of a product, a domain, a data model, a test, a value object and its constraint test, a view, a specification and an endpoint.
then: Expects each to carry its product, domain, aggregate and parent: `EX-LEND-EN01-DM` in aggregate `EX-LEND-A1` under `EX-LEND-EN01`; the value object, view and specification with no parent, in `EX` and `EX-LEND`; and the endpoint under `EX-LEND-CMD01` in aggregate `EX-LEND-A1`.

title: A record with no owner belongs to the one domain that uses it, with what sits under it, and is shared when two or none do
when: With the store's fixture, where Lending's flow step exchanges with the integration, its command is presented in the view, the view's UI component renders it, and a Lending entity's field is typed by the value object, reads `record_scope`; then has a second domain's query presented in the same view and its read model's field typed by a new value object, and a third value object no one uses.
then: Expects the view, integration, UI component and value object, and their requirements, tests, adapter and value type, in Lending; then the view, its requirement, its test and its UI component in no domain, the integration and first value object still in Lending, the new value object in the second domain, the unused one in none, and the view's product unchanged.

title: Every record loads with an ID of its own, under one parent that gives it its product and domain
when: Loads the workspace of a product that holds a record of nearly every kind through the package API.
then: Expects no error, and no two records sharing an ID.

title: An unknown parent is refused once
when: Loads a use case under a domain that does not exist.
then: Expects one foreign-key refusal: domain_id "EX-LEND9" names no domain.

title: A parent that names no record is refused, for every kind's table
when: For each kind, loads the fixture with the record's parent column naming no record.
then: Expects one refusal for it.

title: A missing, unknown or disallowed parent, a second parent or a parent column is refused
when: An aggregate with no domain or an unknown one, an endpoint, table or question with two parents or none, and a product or a kind with no owner given a parent column are loaded.
then: Each is refused; an endpoint under its query and a question under its product load.

title: A row taking another record's ID is refused once
when: Loads a use case test whose ID is a specification's, which links name.
then: Expects one unique-id refusal naming data/specification.jsonl:1, and none of the links to the ID.

title: An ID another record has, of any kind, is refused
when: For each kind, loads a record with the ID of another kind's record, and a second row with the same ID in its own file.
then: Expects a record with another kind's ID refused.

title: refuses an ID that does not start with its parent's or domain's ID
when: Loads a UC requirement whose ID starts with another use case's ID than its parent's.
then: Expects an `id-prefix` refusal naming the parent and the prefix its ID must start with.

title: A link or parent the schema does not allow is refused once
when: Loads a renders link to a UC requirement, and a term with an aggregate_id column.
then: Expects one refusal saying the link names no view, and one column refusal for the column a term does not have.

title: A link whose relation is unknown or not allowed for its two kinds is refused
when: Adds a second `documents` pair (cli_command to integration), then links a CLI command `documents` a UC requirement, a query `calls` a use case, a use case `calls` a domain service, and a use case `teaches` itself.
then: Expects a `relation-pair` refusal saying `TL-LEND-CMD01-CLI (a cli_command) cannot documents TL-LEND-UC01-R01 (a uc_requirement)`, `foreign-key` refusals naming no `domain_service` and no `calls_source (command, query, read_model)`, and an `unknown-relation` refusal for `teaches`.

title: A link from a record of one product to a record of another is refused, whatever the relation; an ID in text is not a link, across products
when: Points a `presents` link at `NX-V01`, a view of a second product.
then: Expects one `link-crosses-product` refusal on `presents` naming `NX-V01` in product NX.

title: Records are related only by links the schema allows between two records of one product
when: Loads the workspace of a product that holds a record of nearly every kind through the package API.
then: Expects every link to join two records of one product by a relation the schema allows.

title: An ID a record names in its text is kept as written, and makes no link
when: Loads records whose text names other records, one of them twice. Loads a use case whose goal names another record twice, and its own ID. Loads a domain whose description names a specification MX-D-SP99 that does not exist, then adds a command with a `checks` link to it. Loads two products, where a use case's text names a record of the other product. Loads a use case whose text names another record of the product by its ID. Loads a domain whose description names the product and the domain by their bare IDs, in plain text and in a code span. Loads a product whose description names a bare product or domain ID in a code span. Loads a use case whose goal names IDs in a code span and in a fenced code block. On a temporary product, sets a requirement's statement naming this product's and another product's IDs, one in a code span. Shows the record and runs lathe check. On a temporary product, sets a requirement's statement to text naming records of this product and another, one in a code span. Shows the requirement and calls check.
then: Expects the text kept as written, no links, and no list of named IDs on a record. Expects a record's text to keep an ID named twice, and its own ID. Expects the text accepted and the link refused as a foreign key. Expects the text kept, no link from the use case, and no problem about the other product's ID. Expects a use case's text naming another record kept as written, and no links. Expects a domain's description naming the product and the domain, in plain text and in a code span, kept exactly. Expects the product's description to keep its code span. Expects the use case's goal to keep the code span `` `EX-LEND-UC02` `` and the fenced block holding EX-LEND-UC94 exactly. Expects the text kept as written, no link added and nothing reported about the IDs. Expects the text shown as written with no links, and no problem about the IDs.

title: A token that is not an ID of this workspace is plain text and no problem
when: Loads a use case whose goal names `STD-CODE-R01` and `SYS-AUTH`, which are no IDs of the workspace. Loads a use case whose goal names an invariant ID no record has, and lists the engine's own checks. Loads text naming IDs that start with a domain's ID and a hyphen but that no record has. Loads text naming IDs with other prefixes, such as `STD-` and `SYS-`. Loads text naming IDs that records have and IDs that none has, then runs every check.
then: Expects text naming IDs that no record has, with unknown prefixes, to be kept and reported by nothing. Expects no problem for a missing rule named in text, and `data-refused` as the engine's only problem of its own. Expects text naming missing IDs with the domain's prefix kept, and no problem about them. Expects text naming STD- and SYS- IDs kept, and no problem about them. Expects no `unknown-id-in-prose` problem, and no problem naming an ID written in another record's text.

title: A use case whose domain is not its result's is an error; one in its result's domain is not
when: Loads the complete product, then the same with a use case whose result is a command of another domain.
then: use-case-result-in-domain is an error naming the use case, its domain and its result's domain, and saying to move it with Move a use case; the complete product has none.

title: A write that puts a use case in a domain other than its result's is refused
when: Adds a use case to a domain with a result of another domain, then changes a use case's result to a command of another domain.
then: Each write is refused by use-case-result-in-domain, naming the result's domain and Move a use case, and changes nothing.

title: A use case's group is its result's aggregate or read model; it moves to a domain that holds its result, and with the aggregate its result is in
when: Reads the group of a command use case, a query use case and a requirement under each, then moves a use case to another domain with a result there, and moves an aggregate that holds results.
then: A command use case's group is its result's aggregate, a query use case's its read model, and a requirement's its use case's; a move to a domain without the result is refused, and a use case moves with the aggregate or read model its result is in.

title: A use case serves the outcomes its aggregate or read model serves, and those of each journey that carries it out
when: Loads the complete product, with an aggregate serving an outcome and a journey serving another.
then: A record reached through a use case of the aggregate serves the aggregate's outcome, and one reached through a step of the journey serves the journey's, each marked with what it is served through.

title: A use case naming one of its product's interfaces or an interface word is a warning; verb and object, or a list, is not
when: Use cases are added that name the command line, the product's Member portal, a page and APIs, that hold a list with a comma, and that join objects with and, refund a fee or grant capital approval.
then: title-breaks-convention warns of each that names an interface word, an interface word inside a longer word (capital) not included, and of none of the others.

title: A use case titled with a CRUD verb over a record or data is not a warning
when: Adds use cases titled Change a product's data, Edit a record, Update the data and Change a check.
then: Expects no title-breaks-convention warning: a command use case's verb is its command's, which use-case-title-off-result reads.

title: A journey naming an interface, holding a list or titled with a CRUD verb over a record is a warning, as a use case
when: Loads the complete product with its journey and four more journeys: one naming the web app, one a list, one a CRUD verb over data, and one goal verb first.
then: Expects a title-breaks-convention warning on each of the first three, saying how a journey is named, and none on the fourth.

title: A title another record of its kind and product has, or one ending with a period, is refused
when: An aggregate titled " loan " is added beside the aggregate Loan, and an invariant is titled with a period at its end.
then: title-unique refuses both aggregates, naming the other; the entity Loan beside the aggregate Loan loads; title-period refuses the invariant.

title: Two rules of one function in one file load, and two rules of one name in two files are refused
when: A second invariant gets a rule titled as the first invariant's rule, in the same file, then in another file.
then: The data with one file loads and counts both invariants as built; title-unique refuses both rules of the data with two files, naming the other.

title: Every name in Lathe and the Tool Library is one to four words with no article first
when: Reads the titles of every name kind in Lathe's own spec and the Tool Library's.
then: None is longer than four words or starts with A, An or The.

title: A domain whose title or code names a technology layer is a domain-named-for-technology warning
when: Adds domains titled Web app, Records (code `DB`), Shop (described as served by its own server) and Guided tours.
then: Expects `domain-named-for-technology` warnings for Web app and for Records, whose code `DB` gives `its code DB says "db"`, and none for Shop, only described as served by its own server, or Guided tours.

title: A query not starting with Get, List or Find is a warning
when: Queries titled Get a loan, find a tool by name, Show overdue loans and Getaway tools are added.
then: query-title-verb warns of Show overdue loans and Getaway tools only.

title: A flow not titled by its use case, in or through, and its interface is a warning
when: A flow is titled in the pattern in several letter cases, then Borrow at the desk; then its use case is renamed.
then: flow-title-off-pattern passes each title in the pattern, warns of Borrow at the desk with the title to give it, and warns again once the use case is renamed.

title: Every policy in Lathe and the Tool Library reads When an event, then its reaction
when: Reads every policy's title in Lathe's own spec and the Tool Library's.
then: Each starts with When, its event, a comma and its reaction.

title: An event title with no past form as its last word or after its first is an event-tense warning
when: Adds events titled Return tool, Loan became overdue, Fee needed and Speed.
then: Expects `event-tense` warnings for Return tool and Speed, and none for Loan became overdue or Fee needed.

title: A specification starting with A, An or The is a warning
when: Specifications titled The tool is free, an active member, Theme is set and Area is open are added.
then: specification-title-article warns of the first two only.

title: A test titled Tests that or Should is a warning, a result is not
when: Use case tests titled Tests that…, Should…, Test whether…, Tests run one at a time and a result are added.
then: test-title-not-a-result warns of the first three only.

title: A code-bound title with whitespace, or an endpoint not titled by its method and route, is refused
when: Titles a command handler `the loan opener` and a table `Loans by member`; titles an endpoint `Borrow a tool`; then adds a data model titled `loan` for TL-LEND-EN02 beside the data model `Loan`.
then: Expects `title-form` to refuse the handler and the table, the handler's message saying a command handler is titled by one identifier exactly as in code, with no whitespace; the endpoint refused by a `check`; and the data model `loan` to load, since code compares exactly.

title: Each rule record is a rule of its rules.ts by the name its refusal carries, and each rule there has its record
when: Reads Lathe's rule records and every rules.ts under lathe/src, with the rule names their refusals carry.
then: Expects each rule record to name a rules.ts that writes a rule of its title, and each rule a rules.ts writes to have a record of that title naming that file.

title: Every kind has at most one lead text, required, and every test a required When and Then and no Given
when: Reads the schema of Lathe's own spec: every kind, part and declaration table's columns and CHECKs.
then: Expects no table with two of statement, goal, meaning and description, every one of them NOT NULL with its trim CHECK, the ten tests with When and Then required and no Given, and no description on the data model, value type, predicate, event type, service, table, flow and flow step.

title: A product kind with an optional lead text, or two, is refused
when: Declares a description field on the fixture's CLI command kind that is not required, then a required description and a statement, then one required description.
then: Expects the first refused as a lead that must be required and the second as a second lead after description, both `product-kind`; the third loads.

title: Data that breaks the model is refused when it is written, across tables
when: With rows that break a key, a CHECK, a foreign key or a validation query (a step fulfilling another use case's requirement, a policy hearing two events, a field with two types, an ID outside its scope, a test with no file), loads or writes each through the store.
then: The store refuses each one then, naming its row and rule, and nothing is saved; no check is left to find it later.

title: A refused command leaves the data and the files as they were
when: A command that breaks the model is applied with others.
then: The whole write is refused and the data and its files stay as they were.

title: A write from the command line or a tool runs the checks first, and answers with the problems it introduced
when: On product TL alone, makes its check strict accepting one warning from the command line, then accepting none, then not strict through the tool.
then: Expects the first refused, since TL has no warning, the second to answer that it introduced no new warnings, and the tool's answer to carry an empty introduced list.

title: The problems a write introduced are the warnings, strict-check and strict-gaps errors not there before
when: Compares a run before a write with one after it, where a warning's words changed with the data, a warning, a strict-check error and a strict-gaps error are new, and an error of another check is new; then a strict-gaps error there before whose count changed.
then: Expects only the new warning and the strict-check and strict-gaps errors, nothing for the strict-gaps error there before, and the answer's text to list them, or to say there are no new warnings.

title: The guard hook refuses an edit of a data file and points at the tools
when: Runs the guard hook on an Edit of `data/product.jsonl`, and on a Write of a relative path in a data folder that `lathe.config.json` names.
then: Expects the permission decision deny, with a reason saying the file is Lathe data to change only with Lathe's MCP tools.

title: The guard hook lets every other edit through, silently
when: Runs the guard hook on a source file, a `.jsonl` file outside the data folder, a data folder outside any Lathe repo, and empty input.
then: Expects exit status 0 and no output each time.

title: The plugin declares the MCP server and the guard hook, and every script they name exists
when: Reads the plugin's `.mcp.json` and `hooks/hooks.json`.
then: Expects the lathe MCP server and one PreToolUse hook, naming `scripts/mcp-server.mjs` and `scripts/guard-data-files.mjs`, both of which exist.

title: A change to the spec is held to its rules whole: a hand edit of a data file is denied pointing at the tools, and a bad write through the MCP tools is refused
when: Reads the plugin's hook declaration and runs its guard script with Write, Edit and MultiEdit of a data file, and with other files; on a temporary product, changes records through the MCP tools.
then: Expects every hand edit of a data file denied pointing at the tools, others passed silently, and a bad write refused.

title: Every interface names one specific command: no two definitions share an ID, a CLI command, an MCP tool or a route, and every command of an aggregate with a slice has its definition
when: Reads every command and query definition, whose identities are generated from Lathe's records, and Lathe's command records.
then: Expects no ID, CLI command, MCP tool or route named by two definitions, and no command of an aggregate with a slice without its definition.

title: The one Button component draws every standalone action: ghost, primary, icon, with an icon, danger, and a link drawn as a button
when: Renders the Button as ghost, primary submit, icon, with the `plus` icon, danger, and as a link to `/DM`; reads the app stylesheet.
then: Expects each its element, type and classes (`button button-ghost`, `button button-primary`, `icon-button`, `button button-ghost button-danger`), a click handled, `buttonClass` giving the same classes, and the stylesheet to style them once: the ghost hover tint, the primary steel fill and a 44 px target on a coarse pointer.

title: Each app aggregate of Exploring and Platform is reached only through its repository, and its handlers, policies and rules are the records' one to one
when: Reads app/src's Exploring and Platform slices and their repository, handler, policy, rule and other code-bound records.
then: Expects only a slice's repository to touch its storage keys, one repository per slice with its load and save, commands importing only their own slice, every code-bound title declared in its file and every command and policy function recorded.

title: Each desktop aggregate is reached only through its repository, and its handlers, policies and channels are the records' one to one
when: Reads desktop/src and the repository, handler, policy, channel and other code-bound records.
then: Expects only repositories to touch the user data folder's files, one repository per slice with a load and a save, commands importing only their own slice, every code-bound title declared in its file, every command and policy function recorded, and every channel recorded once.

title: No kind, column, flag or check records an exception to a rule
when: Reads the schema's tables and columns, Lathe's check rows, the CLI's flags with every command's and query's fields, and the plugin's skills and the READMEs.
then: Expects no table or column that records an exception, a waiver or an opt-out, no check text that exempts, waives or excepts, no flag that skips a rule, and no doc that teaches one.

title: Changes are hard cutovers: no redirect, alias, legacy path or second signature is left
when: The app and the engine sources are scanned.
then: No redirect, alias, legacy path or second addressOf signature is found.

title: What serves no purpose is removed: no unused file, export or dependency
when: Runs knip on `app/`, `lathe/` and `desktop/`.
then: It finds no unused file, export, dependency or binary.

title: No command or icon outlives its purpose: every keymap command is handled and reachable, every named command is in the keymap, and every icon is drawn
when: Reads the app's source, its keymap and its icon table.
then: Expects no command unhandled or unreachable, no command named outside the keymap, and no icon drawn nowhere.

title: No style outlives its purpose: every class selector in the app stylesheets is used in app/src
when: Reads the app's stylesheets and source, and asks whether a class name nothing uses, and `graph-page`, are used.
then: Expects no unused class selector in the app's stylesheets, `a-class-nothing-names` reported unused and `graph-page` used.

title: Each kind is essential or accidental by kind, never by record: a test follows what it proves, a standard its type, an API requirement its product's interfaces
when: Loads the complete example product and reads its kinds, then takes away what provides its internal API's requirement, then makes that API public.
then: Expects each kind's complexity as its stage gives it (essential through interface design and for a test data set, accidental in the technical specification and for an endpoint, as-parent for tests and standard rules, by-type for a standard, by-interface for an API requirement, none only for an open question); the internal API's requirement is accidental and reported until provided, and essential on a public API.

title: An essential record that names technology its kind's group has no business with is a warning, by Lathe's words and the product's own
when: Gives a use case a goal that clicks, a UC requirement that names the Web app, a flow step that clicks and a flow its own interface, a view page buttons rows and JSON, a pattern rule HTTP and JSON, a view test a click, a domain a term Table and a use case that names it, a term Postgres; then gives another domain a term Column and a requirement of the first a column, with and without a database; then lists Postgres and Table among the product's technology words.
then: Expects accidental-in-essential to warn of the goal's and the step's click, the requirement's web app and the view's JSON only; the column, a term of another domain, not at all, the database still; and of Postgres and Table once the product lists them; the complete product draws none.

title: An essential record that names the shape of a technical record, a table written as storage, a file or folder, a route or a command line, is a warning; words that only sound technical are not
when: Gives the complete product a table entity_field kept in lathe/schema/ and an endpoint under /api/, then writes Lathe's own requirements from before their conversion (an entity's fields as its entity_field rows, an interface's POST /api/use-case/<command>, the merge driver's command line, the migrations in lathe/schema/) into its records, words that only sound technical into a use case, a route into an interface and a view; then adds a term entity_field.
then: Expects essential-restates-technical to warn of exactly the four records with the table, file, routes and command line they name, and the term to excuse the table.

title: The same requirement or step statement in three or more use cases or views is a pattern in disguise, read with the names of the aggregates and entities alike
when: Gives two use cases' requirements, one of them twice, the statement Lathe's views gave each aggregate's refused commands with the aggregate's name aside, then the catalog view's requirement the same with an an.
then: Expects no warning for two use cases, then essential-repeated to warn once, on the first record, naming all four records in three use cases or views.

title: A write that adds an essential record, or changes its title or lead, naming technology its kind's group has no business with is refused with the word; one that leaves its text as it was is not
when: On the complete product, changes a use case's goal to click, adds a UC requirement naming the Web app, renames a term Loan row, has a flow step name the Web app and then do so as that interface's variant, has a step click, has a view read from the database, then adds a term Table, a use case naming a table, a second domain with a term Column and a requirement naming a column and then a database, and a pattern rule naming JSON over HTTP, lists Postgres and Table as the product's technology words and writes a use case's actors alone.
then: Expects each leak refused as essential-names-technology with its record and word, the variant step, the view's page, buttons and rows, the term Table and the pattern rule let through until Table is a technology word, and the write that leaves the text as it was let through.

title: The write refusal and accidental-in-essential read one list: every record the check reports is refused when the text it names the word in is written again
when: Loads the complete product with a use case, a UC requirement, a view, a term, an integration and a domain service each naming technology, then writes again, for each, the text the check names the word in.
then: Expects the check to report exactly those records, and each write refused for its record with the word the check named.

title: A change is refused only for the text it sets: a record whose title names technology can still have its lead text changed
when: Loads the complete product with a use case whose title names one of the product's technology words, then changes its goal, then its title to another text with the word, then adds a use case whose goal alone names the word.
then: Expects the change of the goal let through while the check still warns of the title, the change of the title refused for the title alone, and the add refused for its goal.

title: A write that links an essential record to an accidental one, or declares a relation that would, is refused; an outcome may still be measured by a record of an accidental kind
when: Gives the complete product an essential kind of its own with a relation to any record, declares that relation to a table, adds a record of the kind citing a table and then a use case, and declares measured_by from the outcome to a report kind.
then: Expects the declaration and the link to the table refused as essential-links-accidental naming both ends, and the link to the use case and the measured_by declaration let through.

title: An accidental record is a warning until a tooling record generates it, something provides it or a record above it, or it fills a slot serving an essential record
when: From the complete product, whose every accidental record is accounted for, writes a command handler, a UI component and two repositories by hand, takes away the providers of the data store and the generator and what the second repository persists, and fills the slot with the UI component, which builds a view requirement, the repository whose aggregate has a storage requirement and the repository that persists nothing; then takes away the engineering standard's provider and the record that meets its rule, and makes it a quality.
then: Expects accidental-not-accounted-for to warn of the command handler, the repository that persists nothing (it fills a slot but serves no essential record), the generator and the data store; then of the standard and its rule but never its test; then of nothing.

title: Each fill is listed as accidental debt in its domain, and the third fill of one slot makes it a pattern candidate
when: Reads the complete product, whose slot has two fills, then writes a third record by hand and fills the slot with it.
then: Expects the domain's coverage to list both fills as its debt with no pattern-candidate, then pattern-candidate to warn of the slot, naming its three fills.

title: An obligation something outside the product provides is built and proved through its provider
when: Takes away an invariant's rule, its fill and its test, then names the platform integration as the invariant's provider.
then: Expects the invariant neither built nor proved, then built and proved, its provider in its proof list and its chain's build.

title: The store refuses a fill of a record a tooling record generates: a fill is written by hand
when: Loads the complete product with its tooling record also generating a command handler that fills a slot.
then: Expects the store to refuse it with fill-is-hand-written, naming the record, the slot and the generator.

title: A fill serves the essential aggregate it persists, an essential record a product relation links it to in either direction, an outcome it measures, or an essential record under it
when: From the complete product, writes a repository by hand whose aggregate has no storage requirement and fills the slot with it; then adds an accidental product kind with an essential child kind, two product relations to an essential product kind (one each way) and one between two accidental records, and fills the slot with four records of the accidental kind: one linked to an essential record, one an essential record links to, one with an essential record under it, and one linked only to another fill; then has a business outcome measured by that last fill.
then: Expects accidental-not-accounted-for to warn of nothing while the repository persists its aggregate, and of the repository once it persists nothing; then of the fill linked only to another fill, and of no other; and of nothing once an outcome is measured by it.

title: An engineering standard and its rules fill no slot: a rule is accounted for when a record accounted for meets it, and the standard when one of its rules is
when: Takes away the engineering standard's provider, so only the fill that meets its rule accounts for it; then adds a second rule that nothing meets; then makes the record that meets the first rule written by hand and filling no slot.
then: Expects accidental-not-accounted-for to warn of neither the standard nor its rule; then of the second rule only, saying no record that is accounted for meets it; then of the command handler, both rules and the standard, the standard saying no record that is accounted for meets one of its rules.

title: A slot that says why its fills vary by design is no pattern candidate, and the reason is never empty
when: Reads the complete product with a third record written by hand filling its slot, once with the slot's reason that its fills vary by design, once without, and once with a blank reason.
then: Expects no pattern-candidate warning with the reason, one for the slot without it, and the blank reason refused on load.

title: No tracked file names a product Lathe was tried on, a person or a machine's path
when: Every text file `git ls-files` lists is scanned, case-insensitively and by whole word, for the name of a product Lathe was tried on for a client or a collaborator, a person's first name and absolute home or temp paths.
then: None is found outside the allow-list of the author fields, the package name and the repo URL's owner; each finding names its file and line.

title: Lathe's own spec and the Tool Library check clean and wholly proved on every merge into main
manual_reason: Run as the merge gate: before each merge into main, the coordinator runs `npm --prefix lathe run check` on the merged branch and refuses the merge on any error, warning or obligation short of designed, built and proved.
when: Runs `npm --prefix lathe run check` at the repo root on the branch about to merge into main.
then: Expects 0 errors, 0 warnings, and every coverage line at 100% designed, built and proved in both products.

title: A technical record names helper files; the store refuses one on another record, twice, as a record's file or not normalized
when: Loads the complete product with two helper files on a command handler, then with a helper file on a use case, the same helper file on two records, a helper file that is the file of another record, and a path that starts with ./
then: The first loads with no problem and the record holds its helper files; each of the others is refused with the rule it breaks.

title: A source file a record names as a helper file is not a code-file-untraced gap
when: Loads a product with a record's file and two other source files, first with no helper files and then with both named as helper files of the record
then: The two other files are code-file-untraced gaps at first, and no file is a gap once the record names them.

title: A record whose helper file does not exist leaves its obligation unbuilt and is a technical-file-missing warning
when: Loads the complete product with a helper file on an invariant's rule, first with the helper file written and then with it missing
then: The invariant is built while the helper file exists; with it missing the invariant is not built and technical-file-missing names the helper file.

title: An obligation's trace and a change's reach list each helper file with its record
when: Loads the complete product with two helper files on an invariant's rule, then reads the invariant's trace and the reach of a change of the invariant
then: The trace's files and the reach's files list the rule's file and both helper files, each named by the rule.

title: A technical record's page lists its helper files under Traceability
when: Renders the Traceability section of a command handler that names two helper files, and of the same handler with none
then: The section lists both helper files under Helper files, and the handler with none shows no such list.

title: Helper files trace to their record from the command line, and the record builds only while all its files exist
when: On a temporary product with a command handler whose file and two helper files are written, runs lathe check, names the helper files on the handler, runs it again, removes one helper file and runs it again, then reads the requirement's trace.
then: Expects both helper files untraced gaps until named, no gap once named, the missing file reported and the requirement unbuilt, and the trace to list the handler's file and both helper files.
